item.title: A THRILL OF HOPE -All Church Advent Program - 9:45am — Sun Nov 29, 9:45 AM — Divinity School
item.description:
Adults, youth, and children are invited join us to share in A Thrill of Hope!
Advent begins in a weary world, fractured by division and despair. Yet across generations, humanity has clung to the hope of restoration, and God continues to draw near. The Messiah has saved us, is saving us, and will save us. Suffering is not the final word. As we journey through Advent, Christmas, and Epiphany, we watch for God's saving work all around us: healing where there is hurt, courage where there is fear, hope where there is despair. The miracle of Immanuel did not end in Bethlehem. The thrill of hope persists.
Weekly Themes: First Sunday of Advent: Keep Awake Mark 13:24-37 Second Sunday of Advent: Prepare the Way Mark 1:1-8 Third Sunday of Advent: Among You Stands One John 1:6-8, 19-28 Fourth Sunday of Advent: Let It Be with Me Luke 1:26-38 Christmas: Good News of Great Joy Luke 2:1-14 (15-20) First Sunday after Christmas: My Eyes Have Seen Your Salvation Luke 2:22-40 Epiphany: Another Road Matt

item.description:

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Fri Feb 19, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: You Are Here Exhibition — Fri Feb 19, 10:00 AM — Witherspoon Student Center
item.description:
Join the African American Cultural Center to experience ariana Farquharson's You Are Here: Geolocating the Self through the Familiar in the Midst of the Unfamiliar. The exhibition is a speculative, immersive world-building study that invites guests to explore (geo)locating self and home amid a rapidly and frequently changing post-pandemic “new” world. It will be on display in the art gallery at the African American Cultural Center from Oct. 28, 2026, to Feb. 28, 2027. A behind-the-scenes look at the exhibition is set for Nov. 11.
Source: NC State African American Cultural Center

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Sat Feb 20 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: NCMA Online Educator Course: Art and Math — Sat Feb 20
item.description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.
Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art. item.description:
Experience the artistry and expressive range of the Calichi Trio, featuring Duke Music faculty members Ieva Jokubaviciute, piano; Hsiao-Mei Ku, violin; and Caroline Stinson, cello.
The program pairs Johann Nepomuk Hummel's graceful and spirited Piano Trio in E-flat Major, Op. 12, with Dmitri Shostakovich's powerful Piano Trio No. 2 in E Minor, Op. 67. Spanning contrasting musical worlds, these works move from Classical elegance and sparkling interplay to profound intensity, emotional depth, and dramatic urgency.
Together, the three musicians bring this compelling repertoire to life through intimate musical conversation, remarkable ensemble playing, and the rich combination of piano, violin, and cello.

item.title: CEE Seminar - Intelligent Structures: Harnessing Physical Dynamics as a Computational Resource — Mon Nov 23, 12:00 PM — None
item.description: In living systems, the morphology of the body is tightly coupled to the robustness and speed of the sense-assess-respond feedback loop for optimal flight control, maneuverability and many other functions. The concept of "embodiment" emphasizes the significant role that physical shape, mechanical compliance, and multi-functionality can play in facilitating feedback responses that point toward intelligent behavior and control. Using the mathematical framework of reservoir computing, it is possible to harness these intrinsic mechanical behaviors and dynamics from the loading environment as a computational resource. In this presentation, we will evaluate the information processing capacity of several physical reservoir computing systems, including a fluid structure interaction model, a magnetomechanical resonator, and an optomechanical spring network.
